instructions: 1. read the pin Plans/integration-completion/runtime-conformance.json at a Maestro commit this receipt names (HEAD a2920320f8ff24c8b1fe58773f717c4e236d0131 or later, with the archive unchanged) and take runtime.archive.sha256 (759b947aaf546631e573642e5a9c8450adafa74a239e42741766cc1acef05a3e), sha512, bytes and payloadFiles

2. obtain runtime.tgz and its sidecar runtime.tgz.sha256 whose text is '<sha256>  runtime.tgz'; the packager lands them at dist/mega-maestro-runtime/0.32.0/759b947aaf546631e573642e5a9c8450adafa74a239e42741766cc1acef05a3e/ (the directory name is the sha256, a convenience, not an identity); refuse the archive unless its sha256, sha512 and byte count equal the pin, before reading any entry

3. list the entries before extracting: every name under package/, none absolute, none containing .., regular files and directories only (no symlink, hardlink, device or other entry); refuse the archive otherwise

4. extract and read package/manifest.json: its sha256 equals the pin manifestSha256; formatVersion 2, kind maestro-runtime; source.implementation.digest and commit, source.library.inputSha256 and managedPort.entry.sha256 equal the pin; it equals artifact.json beside the archive minus packagedAt, archive and observed

5. check every file in payloadSha256 by sha256 (298 files), refuse any file the map does not name and any named file that is absent; the sha256 of the canonical (sorted-key) JSON of payloadSha256 equals the pin payloadDigest

6. load library/index.js (CommonJS; require() or import from an ES module) in Node >=20; nothing in node_modules is needed (node-pty is an optional peer for PTY routes only) and Electron must not be resolvable; the synthetic harness route further needs a Node that honors --permission, --allow-fs-read, --allow-fs-write, --allow-net and --allow-child-process (observed here under v26.13.0; a Node without --allow-net reports the route unsupported)

7. confirm the bundle says what the manifest says: MAESTRO_LIB_VERSION 0.32.0, MANAGED_CONTRACT_VERSION maestro-managed/1, LOCAL_ENDPOINT_PROTOCOL 1; the 22 managed port exports named in artifact.json are functions

8. negotiate before anything else: negotiateCompatibility(hostCompatibilityProfile({ providers: getAgentIds() }), { contractVersions: [MANAGED_CONTRACT_VERSION], endpointProtocols: [LOCAL_ENDPOINT_PROTOCOL], transport, required }); on the bare bundle only capabilities.negotiate activates and every other required capability is refused by name (missing-required-capability) until the host composes the facade; a refusal is final, never a fallback

9. compose the managed facade the way the pin conformance.invocation.host.compose says a host does (createRunJournal, createContextVerifier, createLocalHostAuthority, createManagedOperations over the host own binding, agent repository and turn port); the consumer then calls the ManagedApi (submit, inspect, cancel, interrupt) with { context, input } and validates its own context with managedContextProblems; the host stamps the peer, a caller never names it; the answers follow conformance.correlation and conformance.semantics (denied, unsupported, unavailable, unknown), which vitest-conformance-archive below shows the archived bytes answer

10. read route support from providerRouteSupport(id) for every id of getVisibleAgentDefinitions(): 55 routes, 11 managed implemented, 44 unavailable; a route read as unsupported is refused, never substituted; the one qualified route is synthetic-harness/node-permission-v1, and what it does and does not qualify is written in artifact.json bootstrap.harness

11. a launch is admitted at the sink: buildDispatchSnapshot(spec, attribution) digested, HostAuthority.admit() asked with a context a verifier of this bundle bound, the lease handed to leaseAdmission() and the gate to startTurn(); the gate re-checks the final snapshot the instant before the spawn and refuses a changed, released, expired or revoked lease with lease-invalid before any effect (harness-turn below observes each)

12. record qualifiedAgainst.maestroRuntimeSha256 = 759b947aaf546631e573642e5a9c8450adafa74a239e42741766cc1acef05a3e (the ARCHIVE digest, never the entry digest b21f1f7d39675d39e8cc2b7468caa7d5a4cfd04b31aa09d64351900f73164f0d) in the adapter pin; scripts/mega-maestro-pair.mjs check --runtime <dir> reads it, and a pair against other bytes is not a pair against this runtime

13. what this runtime does not give: no lease or policy authority (the authority is the host own, bound at the spawn), no provider support, no contracts component (absent: CP-01), no pair; MEGA-RUNTIME-ADAPTER qualifies against this archive, and when a later consumer BUILD names a newer archive the adapter is rebound to that digest and its conformance rerun
